title: Verdant Urgency — Climate-Tech Mission Brief
description: A full-bleed earth-photograph hero for climate-tech founders. Bone-white ranged-left problem copy reads over a muted forest canvas, anchored by a top-right monospace wordmark and a sun-yellow impact-metric chip in the footer.
philosophy: This template exists for founders who believe the problem slide should hit like a physical fact, not a bullet-point list. It refuses decorative gradients and polished brand overlays — the photograph carries the emotional weight while the typography stays raw, angular, and left-aligned. The monospace wordmark signals engineering transparency and anti-corporate conviction over cosmetic credibility. Designed specifically for seed and Series A rooms where mission urgency must be felt in under three seconds.
goodFor: Climate, cleantech, and conservation startup pitch decks
Seed and Series A investor problem-statement hero slides
Bold 3–8 word emission or impact headlines over landscape photography
Footer impact-metric chips such as '2.4 GT CO₂ avoided annually'
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial or KPI review decks
Light-hearted consumer lifestyle or CPG brand pitches
Dense academic regulatory or compliance presentations
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like an urgent field dispatch — a muted, slightly desaturated aerial or ground-level forest photograph shoulders all the emotional weight, while stark ranged-left display copy confronts the viewer with a problem stated as physical fact rather than designed talking point. Composition is asymmetric and left-heavy, with the lone warm-accent footer chip acting as the only punctuation against an otherwise cool, raw canvas. The mood is engineering transparency over cosmetic credibility — anti-corporate, unpolished, and deliberately unadorned. Avoid gradient overlays, decorative borders, centered layouts, and anything that reads as brand polish.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed photograph occupies the entire canvas edge-to-edge with no crop margin or color overlay band. A 12-column grid governs text: the monospace wordmark is pinned top-right in cols 10–12 with a tight top inset; the primary headline runs ranged-left across cols 1–7, positioned at roughly the upper-center vertical third of the canvas. A slim footer strip anchors the bottom edge, with the impact-metric chip locked to the right end of that strip and an optional founder/company label at the left end. Left text margin is a raw 6–7% of canvas width — narrow enough to feel flush and confrontational.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a field report pinned to a wall — urgent, undecorated, and credible through restraint rather than polish. Left-weighted asymmetry dominates: the photograph bleeds across the full right half untouched, acting as silent witness to the data on the left. Compositional rhythm is sparse and vertical — one massive number or short declarative statement, a rule line, then a tight subordinate clause, nothing else. Avoid any softening vignettes, rounded containers, or gradient overlays; the rawness of the image and the angularity of the type must carry the entire emotional argument.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with active content confined to cols 1–7, preserving a wide-open right bleed for the photograph to breathe. A single hairline horizontal rule separates a short all-caps section label from the primary statement block below it. One oversized stat or pull-quote anchors the upper-left zone using dramatic size contrast against a compact two-line supporting descriptor beneath it. Footer row retains the sun-yellow impact-metric chip flush-left and a slide counter flush-right; no header band.
